title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 252 (Appeal to Tribunal against strike-off)

content.overview: A person aggrieved by a Registrar's strike-off may apply to the Tribunal within three years, and a company, member, creditor or workman may apply within the periods in the section, for restoration.
content.glance: A person aggrieved by a Registrar's strike-off may apply to the Tribunal within three years, and a company, member, creditor or workman may apply within the periods in the section, for restoration.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 252 (Appeal to Tribunal against strike-off). A person aggrieved by a Registrar's strike-off may apply to the Tribunal within three years, and a company, member, creditor or workman may apply within the periods in the section, for restoration. The section applies only to the persons, companies, and transactions it names. A filing, approval, or penalty arises only where the section or a rule under it says so. It does not create a power that is reserved to another section or to the Tribunal. Not a verified closure.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: A person aggrieved by a Registrar's strike-off may apply to the Tribunal within three years, and a company, member, creditor or workman may apply within the periods in the section, for restoration.

sections.heading: Explanation
sections.body: If the Tribunal is satisfied that the removal was not justified, or otherwise as the section allows, it may order restoration. The company is then deemed to have continued in existence as if its name had not been struck off. Strike-off itself is section 248.
